Head-to-head probes of the divergences in
tests/reference/tmux_compat/divergences.toml, against the pinned tmux
oracle. One block per entry: the transcript of the probe that proved
what tmux does, run by hand until #384's harness carries it.

== swap-pane -U and -D directions (tmux 3.7c)

A three-pane session, one command per pane so the swap is readable
back. Pane indices start at 1 on this machine's tmux.conf.

$ tmux -S probe.sock new-session -d -s probe 'sh -c "echo A; sleep 999"'
$ tmux -S probe.sock split-window -t probe 'sh -c "echo B; sleep 999"'
$ tmux -S probe.sock split-window -t probe 'sh -c "echo C; sleep 999"'
$ tmux -S probe.sock list-panes -t probe -F '#{pane_index} #{pane_start_command}'
1 "sh -c \"echo A; sleep 999\""
2 "sh -c \"echo B; sleep 999\""
3 "sh -c \"echo C; sleep 999\""

-U from the middle pane (index 2):

$ tmux -S probe.sock select-pane -t probe.2
$ tmux -S probe.sock swap-pane -U -t probe
$ tmux -S probe.sock list-panes -t probe -F '#{pane_index} #{pane_start_command}'
1 "sh -c \"echo B; sleep 999\""     <- B came UP: -U is the pane above
2 "sh -c \"echo A; sleep 999\""
3 "sh -c \"echo C; sleep 999\""

-D from the same pane, putting it back:

$ tmux -S probe.sock swap-pane -D -t probe
$ tmux -S probe.sock list-panes -t probe -F '#{pane_index} #{pane_start_command}'
1 "sh -c \"echo A; sleep 999\""
2 "sh -c \"echo B; sleep 999\""     <- B went DOWN: -D is the pane below
3 "sh -c \"echo C; sleep 999\""

The wrap agrees: -U from the topmost pane swaps with the bottom one
(the previous pane cyclically), which is also in the transcript of
the first attempt at this probe.

tmux(1) swap-pane: "-U: swap the active pane with the pane above (or
previous)", "-D: swap the active pane with the pane below (or next)".
